description: Canonical merge, CI, and branch policy for the ICN monorepo. Agents must not hardcode these values — read this file.

merge.strategy_note: The set of valid merge strategies is CLOSED and owned by the CONSUMER'S CODE, never by this file: merge | squash | rebase. A consumer must map the value through that closed set and reject anything else — it must never form a command flag by prefixing this text with `--`. Adding a value here does not make it valid. This is stated because a consumer that interpolated the value directly would let a policy saying `admin` reconstruct `--admin`, and for a stacked PR the base that supplies this file can be contributor-controlled (icn#2656 review).

exception.applies_to: Subtree import commits (a squashed subtree add)
exception.note: The one documented departure from default_strategy. Structured so a consumer can SELECT it: as prose it could be displayed but never applied, so the exempt category was squash-merged anyway. The category is the merge commit produced by a squashed subtree import (`git subtree add --squash`); `applies_to` describes it without spelling a command, because operative fields may not hold command-shaped strings. Whether a PR is a subtree import is not mechanically derivable, so selecting this is an operator statement and the reason must be stated explicitly at merge time. `strategy` is subject to the closed set in strategy_note exactly like default_strategy.

merge.agent_tooling_check_note: Runs on all PRs via .github/workflows/agent-drift-check.yml. Add to GitHub branch protection via: gh api repos/InterCooperative-Network/icn/branches/main/protection to make merge-blocking.
merge.required_checks_live_source_note: A SYMBOLIC source, not a command. The consumer's code knows how to read branch protection for the branch it is actually merging into; it must not be handed a command string from data, and must not assume `main` — this field previously baked `branches/main/protection`, which is wrong for any non-primary base.

not_deferred.note: An ordinary merge must complete or refuse, never arm something to happen later. A bare `gh pr merge` against a merge-queue base ENQUEUES the PR; a PR another actor already armed with auto-merge will merge on its own once requirements are met. Either way a consumer reporting `Not merged` would be stating a complete outcome while a deferred merge stayed live. Detect and report; do not disarm another actor's request.

ready_when.note: The structured definition of `this PR is ready for an ordinary merge`. NOT YET CONSUMED by any skill or program: this entry is the schema owner, landed ahead of the evaluator that will read it, because that evaluator must load policy from its target's PINNED BASE COMMIT and therefore cannot depend on a field that exists only on the candidate branch (icn#2651/#2656). Until that consumer exists, this is a declaration of intent validated by scripts/check-merge-policy-schema.py, not a live gate.
ready_when.allowlist_note: Allowlists, not denylists: a denylist admits any state nobody enumerated. `null` is listed in review_decision_allowlist on purpose — it is what this repo reports today (required_approving_review_count: 0) and admitting it by omission would be a fail-open. No pending state is allowlisted at all: pending is not ready. A consumer must treat a required check it cannot account for as NOT ready, including one GitHub never reported. `merge_state_status_in` is the SOLE owner of which merge states are ready: it admits only CLEAN and UNSTABLE, and UNSTABLE only because non-blocking checks do not gate — the required set is proved green separately by required_check_conclusion_allowlist, so UNSTABLE cannot smuggle a red required check past this gate. A separate `unstable_is_mergeable` boolean used to own that same decision; it was removed in icn#2658 review because two owners can disagree and nothing would notice. DIRTY, BLOCKED, BEHIND, HAS_HOOKS and UNKNOWN are not ready states and are rejected by the validator, not merely absent here.
ready_when.field_note: `MERGEABLE` is a value of the `mergeable` field (GraphQL `MergeableState`: MERGEABLE | CONFLICTING | UNKNOWN). `mergeStateStatus` is a DIFFERENT enum (`MergeStateStatus`: DIRTY | UNKNOWN | BLOCKED | BEHIND | UNSTABLE | HAS_HOOKS | CLEAN) and never takes the value MERGEABLE. Until icn#2651 the admin-bypass condition compared `mergeStateStatus` against `MERGEABLE`, which no PR can ever satisfy, so the documented exception was unreachable as written. That defect is gone twice over: the values that must agree now live here as structured data checked against pinned enums, and the human exception no longer restates them at all. Re-verify with: gh api graphql -f query='{__type(name:"MergeStateStatus"){enumValues{name}}}'
ready_when.consumer_contract_note: The planned ordinary-merge evaluator (icn#2651 stage B) may act on this gate ONLY when the PR's base equals `branch.primary`. Pinning a base commit makes its policy IMMUTABLE, not AUTHORITATIVE: for a stacked PR the base may be a contributor-controlled feature branch that can set its own required_checks and ready_when. Restricting the primitive to the primary branch is what makes the pinned base OID also the trusted policy revision; stacked merging belongs to the separate stack flow. Any future generic support must separate TARGET BASE from TRUSTED POLICY AUTHORITY rather than making this schema more rigid. Relatedly, an evaluator executed from the candidate worktree is candidate-controlled: stage B must run from a trusted locus whose executable code does not come from the PR under evaluation.

admin_bypass.eligibility_note: THIS OBJECT IS NOT AUTHORITATIVE FOR ELIGIBILITY. `authoritative_source` alone defines when a human maintainer may admin-merge, and it requires more than PR state: local verification matching the required scope, proof that non-required failures are pre-existing on the primary branch, and a documented exception. Until icn#2658 review this file carried a structured `requires` object that encoded only the PR-state and queue-starvation prerequisites, so a maintainer following it could believe an admin merge was permitted while the ADR said wait or fix. The fix is ONE OWNER, not a fuller copy: duplicating all five conditions here would recreate exactly the drift this work exists to eliminate, and the copy would rot the moment the ADR changed. Consult the ADR. If it cannot be consulted, no bypass is inferred.
admin_bypass.fail_closed: Absence of evidence that a runner is stalled is not evidence that it is. An unreadable or unavailable authoritative_source means NO bypass, never a default-allow.
admin_bypass.consumer_note: No agent program consumes this object. The ordinary-merge evaluator planned in icn#2651 performs ordinary merges only and has no privileged path; it does not read, evaluate or route to this exception. This file makes no claim about any other skill — a claim about `every skill` cannot be made true by a data file.

auto_merge.use_when: A required check is still pending (not failed)
auto_merge.note: SEMANTIC, not a command. Until icn#2651 this read `gh pr merge <N> --auto --squash`, duplicating default_strategy; the repair replaced it with `gh_flags: ['--auto']`, which was worse in a different way — arbitrary CLI authority encoded as data. A contributor-controlled base could set `['--admin']` or `['--disable-auto']` and the validator accepted it (icn#2658 review). The consumer's CODE owns the mapping from `enabled` to `--auto`, exactly as it owns the strategy mapping. Policy declares intent; only code spells flags. NOT for the ordinary-merge evaluator, which merges now or refuses — this documents the batch/stack flows.

readiness_definition: Every check in `merge.required_checks` passed (the list is the count; do not restate one here)
Branch is up-to-date with main (strict mode)

The `mergeable` / `mergeStateStatus` gate is defined structurally by `merge.ready_when` — read that field, do not restate it here. Until icn#2651 this line duplicated the enum values in prose, and a checker had to parse English to notice when the duplicate drifted.

workspace.note: Run cargo from icn/ (the Cargo workspace root, contains Cargo.toml). The repo root itself has no Cargo.toml.
